title: Using RPG Maker as a support for a physical RPG

posts.author: EloiHunter
posts.body:
I have a tabletop RPG in mind but I want to give it a bit of life. My idea is to use a design program to create battle animations, events, etc. Let me explain the idea. I bought Final Fantasy 14 TTRPG, which is like a D&D but from the Final Fantasy world, and I want to use RPG Maker as an assistant on several screens.
1st screen: it would be the screen that acts as a board, where we put the figures. On this screen the stage will be shown in aerial view and the attack animations.
2nd screen: it would be the game control screen, turn control, selection of player and enemy attacks, I would virtually move the characters, I would put the buffs/debuffs, among many other things. In essence it would be the Dungeon Master screen.
3rd screen (if possible): it would be to show the fight RPG style, enemies on one side and the players on the other, life bars, etc., apart from the events like a visual novel.
My question is to what extent can this be done? Can it be done with VX or XP?

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
It's better to get a more modern maker. Even MV is very cheap when there's a sale.
You could keep your project open and set the board by placing player/monster events on a map. Then in playtest you take turns to move around on the map by switching the gameplayer and the events with scripts.
I'm a bit confused since first you talk about making attacks on the board and then about a standard jrpg battle screen. Just having battles is easy, launch them from the events. But if you meant that the battlers would automatically fight many turns, using commands you'd previously selected on the map, that's a lot harder to set up, but not impossible. Not beginner friendly though. You could also look up some SRPG plugins.

posts.author: EloiHunter
posts.body:
Thanks for answering and sorry for the confusion, I made it short so it wouldn't be too much to read, I'll explain myself further to fix this.
I'll start by saying that I'm a neophyte in this field, the project started with the idea of making a program from scratch with a friend who is a programmer and also a Dungeon Master creating his own game system from scratch, but due to lack of time he can't help me, so while researching I remembered that I have the VX and the XP as a gift and I thought about using them as a base, but if you don't have the resources I'll wait for the MV or the SRPG to be cheaper to buy them, if you know of a more specific category to present this case and get more help I would appreciate it.
The original idea was a program that you could load images, animations and text and organize it in such a way that it would act a bit like RPG Maker when creating the world (as far as a friend explained to me if that's how RPG Maker works, that's why I was interested in using it as a base later), the program would be divided into 2 main parts, the editor and the game, the editor would have several databases where it saves images for characters, maps, attacks and whatever was needed, a data library such as objects with their statistics, skills with their effects and characters, NPCs and monsters with their abilities, a music and sound library to give atmosphere. Finally, a conversation scene editor like in a visual novel to tell the story, I'm sure I've left something out, but now I can't remember everything. When all this was built to work as a story, a separate file would be generated so that it could be saved and played in the future or shared with other users of this program. But all this part was forgotten when the team I had stopped having time to work. The part I want to do now is the player, I'll start with the screens, as well explained as I can.
The first screen is the DM screen, it's the one I'll use to start the game, it starts by selecting the campaign I've saved, for example I'd have the main story, some secondary story, special missions, it wouldn't just be the main campaign, I'm talking about having several simultaneous games saved each with a series of scenarios that can be common or not, basically like starting a game in an extra mode apart from the main game. So it's possible that instead of the game settling instead of the 8 that we would play, we could be less because we would have to select the number of players. So in this first DM window we would have a campaign selector, the number of players for it and the difficulty level. The second window would be to choose the characters that we will play, each one with their corresponding role within the group (tank, healer, DPS), this part we comment on a modification but I doubt that it is possible, which is that we have an application to select and control the characters on the mobile using the computer as a server, it is crazy, but if something else can be done and the DM does not have to enter data, well, this is something exceptional so I continue with the important thing. During the game the DM screen has to have several things to control the game, a map with boxes to be able to locate the players as if they were Fire Emblem characters, the list of entities (players, enemies, NPCs, objectives to interact with either by attacking or taking), the order of the turns, the life of everyone, the wear and tear of the equipment, some pop-up notification that a requirement has been met, things like these.
The second screen would be the stage. The idea is to put it on a television lying on the table, so we would put the figures on it. Here we would see the stage, the grid, some markers that would act as a reference for the locations of the figures, a touch like destroy this object or the monster does not receive damage, the animations of the attacks like if the wizard throws a fireball from the location where the wizard is, a projectile comes out towards the target and if the attack is an area, then mark the area to be able to leave it.
The third screen would be on the wall, and it would be the one that fulfills a double objective, during the fights it shows the typical classic RPG fights, using the example of the wizard, if a projectile is shown on the table, that same projectile will appear hitting the monster making it blink and the damage done, it will also show the life bars of the enemies and the heroes, as well as the corresponding buffs and buffs (I have done this in 3D printing for the base because it seemed nice to me and one has the character that seems to have come out of the Mardi Gras of New Orleans with so many circles as he is wearing, that moment becomes chaotic because he does not even remember when he has to take off a stat, whether good or bad). On the other hand, it would be the screen where the NPCs are narrating things, it has nothing more.
Now I will explain a little about the mechanics of the game. Once the mission, difficulty and characters have been selected, we would enter the world. I don't know whether to show the entrance animation or not. We will see later. I will narrate an improvised game as an example. We are in the adventurers guild, dead table screen a table with drinks as if we were sitting at it, wall screen shows a tavern background, background music and DM screen shows the general settings of the screen, it shows some buttons that control the cinematics text forward, text back and history, we press text forward, on the even screen an NPC who manages the guild appears with a mission for us, if we continue pressing the text forward button she tells us about the mission she wants us to do, then we decide if we do it or not, at this moment several options would appear on the screen, the players decide and the master marks the decision on his screen, (on this occasion my friends' chaotics said they did not accept the mission and I put the receptionist in tyrant mode threatening them that they would have to pay a fine if they rejected the mission, among other things...), the players accept and we change the scenario to an open field, this mission consists of a first part of tracking, I press a button event and select perception, a window will appear for the challenge and I suggest they roll by perception, the idea is that the game faces the difficulty that I have imposed on the players' base (within their character sheet) + the die bonus that I have to write inside that window, if they pass it on the map some little lights will appear to investigate, when they get closer on the wall a description of what they have found will be shown, this system will have modifications in the future so that in case I have not prepared anything and they use perception, they find random things, like coins, herbs, etc. On this occasion they have found some footprints, they follow them and a combat begins, on the master screen a pop-up window would appear with a combat notification, on this occasion I would recommend them to roll the die by perception, in the future I would put a little sound to warn them and have them roll it, if they roll the die and pass the test avoid the surprise attack if not the enemies' turn begins. This is where the master's work begins, as this entire adventure is already written, in the Master's window the window of the order of the turns will appear according to the initiative of each character, what he will do in his turn, his life bars, the altered states and a bar called LB that will be charged according to the damage that the heroes do, the enemies already have an order for the attacks, the idea is that they move and position themselves to launch those attacks as they would do in a game, in the players' turn, we would start with the tank, in his first action of the turn he would move and launch two attacks the first is a sword attack and the second he will launch provoke so that the enemies focus on him, in the master's screen it would be to choose the tank he would select that he would move, mark the location on his map and that mark will appear somewhat more transparent on the table screen to verify that it is there where the player wants to move, the next thing is the attack, select the sword attack, and the math begins, first roll to hit, hit rate of the attack + the enemy's evasion and comparing it that the result of the die, if the result is lower the attack fails in this case we will give him the victory, the attack does damage, well another math, damage + modifiers + weaknesses - defenses = lost life, enemy blinking on the table and wall screens and loss of life, now it's time to provoke the same hit roll, it hits, and adds a status to the enemy so that they focus on him. On the wizard's turn instead of moving he throws a fireball and uses concentration, we skip combat, with concentration instead of moving he prepares to launch an attack in the middle of the enemy's turn, we skip the rest of the combats and on the enemy's turn we have the tank's provoke interruptions so the attacks are focused on him, enemy 1 (provoked) attacks, tank takes damage, enemy 2 attacks but the wizard uses an attack that interrupts him, enemy 3 uses acid and poisons the tank, as the DM has seen this, well in the same way, enemy 1 starts the turn and presses a button to stop the next phase, enemy turn 2 wizard interrupts well the DM presses a button as if the wizard had an interruption on the enemies' turn, it's like a turn for the wizard, he casts a spell acts like an attack, and jumps to the third enemy, this poisons the tank, which at the end of the tank's turn he loses life, after x turns if healing magic is not applied this disappears.
End of the fight, heroes win, victory music and on to the next thing. Since I don't have the complete rules yet, I don't have much idea of how the leveling up or dropped items work. It's not my fault, the complete manual costs as much as the board game and these people decided to sell it at the end of February, 8 months after the game's release. I only have the basic one with 3 stories.
If you've read this far, thank you. I know it's a huge project, so before making any purchase moves, I'd rather know if RPG Maker will comply with this or not, so I need all the information I can get.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I don't think anyone is going to be willing to read such a dense wall of text.
Having skimmed through it, I'd say if you are new to RPG Maker, this is not going to be something you can do. There are a lot of custom parts that would need to be programmed. Additionally, using the ruby engines, VX Ace and earlier, would have trouble rendering at high resolutions and across multiple screens.
A sort of hacky way I can imagine doing the multiscreen thing without making companion apps that talk to each other would basically be to get 3 screens with the same resolution (for example 3 1080p screens), then set the render resolution to be 3x the length of the total resolution of the screen.
Then you can just set pictures on the left side of the screen and right side of the screen.
The problem doing this in VX Ace and earlier is that they do not support high resolutions; they don't even support 1080p, let alone 5760px (3x the length of 1080p)
This is just the technical part of the display. Some of the other things sound like they would need to be custom programmed. Out-of-the-box, a lot of this cannot be done simply, or can be done but would likely require experience with the software and not something for a beginner.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: Ah when I read your opening post I totally didn't register that you meant like actually using 3 different screens LOL. But yeah, read TheAM-Dol's answer.
